findings.claim: statedPartners unions a partner's rows across every cited finding that prints the same name. So an issue #477 'in several of her orders' finding inherits an interaction rule finding's rows for a shared order display, and that one order is credited by the prose rule. This contradicts the residue the PR documents in this javadoc (lines 269-271) and in ADR Decision 100's #555 amendment (docs/adr.md:7810): that #477's orders 'carry none' and are 'stated only by its printed name'.
findings.evidence: Throwaway test in CitedFindingPartnerCompletionTest using the PR's own OverShippedData over the shipped KB. Question 'Can I give her warfarin?'; orders 'Metronidazole 500mg tablet' and 'Metronidazole 0.75% gel' with ATC codes the KB does not carry (Z99ZZ01/Z99ZZ02), so the interaction chip takes the ORDER rung. Finding 4 partners=[Metronidazole 500mg tablet] rows=[[DDInter1202, DDInter1203]]; finding 5 (#477) partners=[Metronidazole 500mg tablet, Metronidazole 0.75% gel] rows=[[], []]. Answer citing only [5] ('metronidazole is in two of her active orders [5]'): both orders appended, {named=2, stated=0}, as documented. Answer citing [4] and [5] ('interacts with active order Metronidazole [4], and metronidazole is in two of her active orders [5]'): only 'active order Metronidazole 0.75% gel' appended, {named=3, stated=2}. So the #477 finding's tablet order counted as stated through finding 4's rows. With the real ATC codes (J01XD01/D06BX01) the interaction finding prints 'Metronidazole' and the shapes do not collide, which is why the PR's residue case stays green. Probe reverted with git checkout.

verdict: Ready to merge. The fix resolves #555 on all three of the issue's question shapes, through the drug-name prose rule over rows carried structurally from the chip. That is the sibling pattern (namesTheEndedOrderDrug, namesTheFindingsSubject). The only finding is a non-blocking mismatch between the documented #477 residue and what the cross-finding row union does.

Traced the map keys at both rule-chip write sites (drug-in-play arm partnerName at DrugSafetyValidator ~4610, screening arm chipPartnerName at ~8897, collapseSharedMechanisms' merge) against what interactionWarning puts into namedPartners: aligned at every site. Checked which other chip factories populate namedPartners: classOnlyInteraction is empty, substanceInSeveralActiveOrders, ordersSharingASubstance and conditionMediated carry none. Checked that rowsOfSubstance draws from the order-resolved entries, and that matchesText folds lower-case prose itself (same call shape as namesTheEndedOrderDrug). Ran CitedFindingPartnerCompletionTest at head: 14/0. Mutation M1 (prose arm disabled in statedPartners) reddened the 4 new positive cases: alprazolam on search and on searchStreaming, the screening case, the merged case. Mutation M4 (merged chip's row union dropped) reddened only the merged case. Both match the PR body's mutation claims. Pass 2, outward: the cross-finding union in statedPartners produced F1, driven through the real search(). Checked InteractionClaimPairFidelityCheck, which keeps containment by design: the issue's case has the order display among the bridge names. Checked the composed module-answer path at LlmInferenceService ~921, where the composed text prints the label itself. Checked exception safety of the now service-calling withUnstatedPartnersNamed: rows exist only once the dataset is loaded, so getAll returns the cached entries. Ran ArchitectureGuardTest, ProjectInstructionsGuardTest, SharedMechanismChipCollapseTest, InteractionClaimPairFidelityTest and FindingPartnerLogDisclosureTest: all green. Pass 3: callers of the widened RecordMapping constructor (git grep 'new RecordMapping(' gives 0 in omod/src and 87 in api/src as the positive control). Wire exposure of getFindingPartnerRows: same posture as the public getFindingBridgeNames and getFindingSubjectRows, which no serializer reads. Performance: one getAll() id scan per partner, the sibling namesTheFindingsSubject's cost. Pass 3 found nothing substantive.

A live reproduction against a running OpenMRS and llama-server: none is available. The fix was verified only through the module's tests, which stub the model.
notes: The approach was weighed against two alternatives. Stripping the label's parenthetical was rejected at plan review, correctly, under reference CLAUDE.md 'Matching a drug name'. Crediting the order displays in getFindingBridgeNames by containment cannot attribute a display to a partner index in the screening arm, where both drugs are her orders. The chosen structural rows are the more precise option and follow the existing getFindingSubjectRows precedent. F1 can be fixed either way: evaluate the prose arm per finding (rows only for the finding that carries them), or keep the union as 'an order is one key' and correct the #477 residue wording in the javadoc and the ADR. The working tree was restored and git status --porcelain is clean.
